The replayr_movie S3 class

Source: R/replayr_movie.R
replayr_movie.Rd

An imported recording with assigned input streams. Recordings whose polls have unassigned ports use replayr_poll_stream. A replayr_movie is a list with the following elements:

Details

header

Named list of header key-value pairs lifted from the source file. The synthetic _format entry records which parser produced the movie, such as "fm2", "bk2", or "ltm".

commands

Integer vector with one entry per observation. Per-observation emulator command bits, where the format uses them.

inputs

Logical 3D array, dimensions (observations, players, buttons). TRUE means the button was held at that observation.

analog

List of numeric channel matrices, one per player. Rows align with inputs; columns are named by the keys of channel_layout(), and units depend on the format.

analog_mode

Selected representation label. Numeric source values are retained in every mode.

stick_modes

Named left/right choices: "raw", "cardinal4", "cardinal8", "angle", or "angle+magnitude".

button_ids, button_keys, layout_version

Stable control identities and registry version for the compact input columns.

stick_values

Selected numeric stick channels, one matrix per player; accessed with stick_channels().

source_path

Path the movie was loaded from, or NA. ZIP imports also retain the selected source_member.

events, timing, input_events

Where present, source-specific event records and timing. See the format-specific reader.

button_mnemonics

Character vector. One mnemonic per third-dimension slot of inputs; source-defined controls may use multi-character labels.

button_names

Character vector. Friendly labels paired with button_mnemonics.

The accessors name control columns by button_keys; mnemonics and labels are further columns of button_layout().

Use n_observations(), n_players(), n_buttons() to read the array shape and player() to extract one player's buttons as a 2D matrix. summary() counts held observations and activations per control, as.data.frame() returns one row per observation, and [movie[i]][subset-recording] selects observations and keeps the class.

See also

read_movie(), universal_buttons()

Examples

movie <- read_movie(system.file("extdata", "sample.dtm", package = "replayr"))
class(movie)
#> [1] "replayr_movie"
# Observations, controllers and controls.
dim(movie$inputs)
#> [1] 3600    1   12
names(movie$header)[1:5]
#> [1] "_format"       "Platform"      "romId"         "rerecordCount"
#> [5] "frameCount"   
movie
#> <replayr_movie [dtm] observations=3600 players=1 buttons=12 source=sample.dtm>
#> Header keys: Platform, romId, rerecordCount, frameCount, inputCount, inputCountRole, availablePollCount, pollCountDifference, ...
#> P1 active observations: dpad_right=900, dpad_left=900, dpad_down=900, dpad_up=900, start=6, b=900, a=450, x=288
# The accessors and methods work on a selection as on the whole recording.
summary(movie[1:600])
#> dtm recording sample.dtm: 600 controller polls, 1 controller, 12 controls
#> Controls active at least once:
#>  controller        key  name held activations
#>           1 dpad_right Right  150           5
#>           1  dpad_left  Left  150           5
#>           1  dpad_down  Down  150           5
#>           1    dpad_up    Up  150           5
#>           1      start Start    1           1
#>           1          b     B  150          26
#>           1          a     A   75          16
#>           1          x     X   48          13
#> Numeric channels:
#>  controller           key          name min max missing
#>           1  left_trigger  Left trigger   0   0       0
#>           1 right_trigger Right trigger   0   0       0
#>           1        left_x  Left stick X  58 198       0
#>           1        left_y  Left stick Y  58 198       0
#>           1       right_x Right stick X 128 189       0
#>           1       right_y Right stick Y 128 128       0
